# Pull Request Rules

## General

- The PR title needs to be clear and human-readable.
- Small, incremental patches are better than gigantic code submissions. Huge changes need to be discussed with the RetroDECK Team via our social channels.
- The RetroDECK Team needs to understand your PR as well, so be prepared to explain in your own words why this PR is needed and what you hope to achieve. You may be asked about the full PR or just specific sections and you should be able to explain whichever comes up.
- We currently don't accept submissions to our ES-DE fork. All ES-DE changes should happen upstream, simply submit your ideas to ES-DE's GitLab.
    - This is a general recommendation: if an improvement can be contributed directly to upstream, that's always the preferred path.
- **Most importantly:** You must understand every line of code you are submitting.

## LLM Rules

- Fully **automated PRs** submitted through external agents are **not allowed**.
- We currently do not accept co-authored PRs written by AI.
- You may use an LLM as a light writing assistant to help draft and paste the explanation of outside of your PR in order to:
    - Overcome language barriers.
    - Correct grammar, spelling, punctuation, sentence structure and capitalisation.
    - Communicate more effectively, for example, by helping with markdown formatting.
- If the RetroDECK Team has questions about your PR, you are **not allowed** to set up **automated responses** to those questions, as that would be considered rude and neither gentlemanly nor ladylike.
    - However, you may draft your response and refine it using the light writing assistant rules outlined above to help you convey your message clearly. We simply want to talk to **you** not to an AI or a bot. In other words, don't say: "Hey AI, reply to the RetroDECK Team for me plx." That would count as an automated response and not elegant.
